title.narrative: Project Research_Reinforcing Social Cohesion and Resilience of Conflict Affected Communities

description.narrative: Plateau State, located in central Nigeria, is situated along the major religious faultline in the country, dividing the largely Muslim North from the predominantly Christian South. Over the years, this region has experienced a disturbing increase in intercultural and interreligious violence, resulting in the tragic loss of over 10,000 lives since 1992 alone (Human Rights Watch, 2013). Thousands of these casualties have occurred since 2010, highlighting a growing trend of intolerance where individuals are targeted solely based on their ethnic or religious affiliations. The complex interplay of social, religious, and political forces within Nigeria's federal structure exacerbates tensions and divisions. This situation has made the younger generation in Nigeria increasingly susceptible to violent extremism. The lack of effective leadership and alternative narratives further contributes to the region's instability, creating opportunities for further hostilities, particularly in the herders and farmers conflict.
